```markdown
# Design: `breaking` flag on release-notes bullets

Source: deferred item 7 (disposition: Design). Approved by partner.

## Problem
`release-notes` writes one bullet per merged pull request. Breaking changes are
not marked, so readers can't spot them and `announce` can't put them first.

## Decision
Mark breaking changes with a leading `[breaking]` tag on the bullet.

We rejected adding a third " — breaking: yes" part. That would change the
bullet's shape for every entry. With the tag, untagged bullets parse exactly as
before, so existing release notes stay valid.

## Format
    [breaking] <title> — <rest>     # breaking change
    <title> — <rest>                # unchanged

The tag is literal, lowercase, at the very start of the bullet text, followed
by one space.

## Changes
1. **`skills/release-notes/SKILL.md`**: when the pull request has the
   `breaking` label, start its bullet with `[breaking] `.
2. **`skills/changelog-check/parse.py`**: before the existing " — " split,
   strip a leading `[breaking] ` and set `breaking=True` on the entry
   (default `False`). The two-part limit on the split stays as it is.
3. **`skills/announce/SKILL.md`**: list entries with `breaking=True` first in
   the post, then the others in their original order.
4. **Test in `skills/changelog-check/`**: one tagged bullet parses with
   `breaking=True` and the tag removed from the title. One untagged bullet
   parses as before with `breaking=False`.

## Out of scope
- Other tags or severities.
- Rewriting existing release notes.
```
